questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis presents with confusion, asterixis, and lethargy. His serum ammonia level is elevated. A diagnosis of hepatic encephalopathy is made, and appropriate treatment is initiated. Which of the following statements regarding the management of hepatic encephalopathy is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Lactulose acts by acidifying the gut lumen and converting ammonia (NH₃) to non-absorbable ammonium (NH₄⁺)

options.label: B
options.text: Rifaximin is a poorly absorbed oral antibiotic that reduces intestinal ammonia production and is preferred in recurrent episodes

options.label: C
options.text: Oral neomycin kills urease-positive bacteria in GIT and thus reduces the production of ammonia

options.label: D
options.text: Proton pump inhibitors are first-line therapy in hepatic encephalopathy as they reduce gastric acid and ammonia absorption
